type.description: The kind of database. postgres is the only one this version runs.

dsn.description:
A libpq connection string or URL. It carries a password, so render it
from an environment variable. There is no default: a daemon without a
database fails at startup rather than writing somewhere else.

postgres.description: The Postgres the tables live in. Required when type is postgres.

store.description:
Where the rollup tables live. `sqlflow rollup run`, `install` and
`verify` connect to it. ddl, serve, check and test never read it, so a
test run cannot reach this database.

id.description:
ID is the operator's name for this instance. The receiver files a
bundle under it, so reporting without one cannot be filed at all.

report_to.description:
ReportTo is where bundles are posted. Empty means reporting is off,
which is the ordinary case for an instance with no control plane.

key.description:
Key is the credential the control plane issued. It is the private half
of an Ed25519 keypair and belongs in an environment variable, which the
template renders in.

interval_seconds.description: IntervalSeconds is how often to report. Absent means the default.

labels.description:
Labels are the operator's own, copied into every report, so a fleet
can be filtered by region, tenant or environment.

At most 10. A key is lower case, starts with a letter, and is at most
32 characters of [a-z0-9_]. A value is at most 64 characters. A key
the bundle already carries is refused: id, name, version, commit,
arch, config_hash, source_type, sink_type, handler_type.

They are fixed for the life of the process: a receiver stores a series
per field, and a set that changed mid-run would split one instance's
history in two.

turbostats.description:
Where this instance reports itself: the block `sqlflow run` and
`sqlflow serve` take.

name.description:
Names the rollup in messages. Lowercase letters, digits and
underscores, starting with a letter.

table.description: The source table. The generator never creates it.

time_column.description: The timestamptz column holding each row's bucket.

grain.description: The source's bucket width, such as 1m.

dimensions.description:
The source's key besides time. A dimension set with exactly these
dimensions can serve the source grain directly.

source.description: The table the pipeline writes at the finest grain.

from.description:
The grain this one is re-merged from: the source grain or a narrower
declared grain whose width divides this one's.

grains.description:
Each coarser grain, keyed by its width such as 5m, 1h or 1d, and the
grain it is built from.

name.description: Names the set and prefixes its tables.

dimensions.description: Source dimensions the set keeps. Empty keeps one row per bucket.

type.description:
sum, min, max, last or count_buckets. last keeps the value of the
latest finer bucket. avg, gauge and histogram are reserved and refused
until a later version generates them.

column.description:
The source column the measure reads. Required for sum, min, max and
last; refused for count_buckets, which counts source buckets.

numeric.description:
How a sum is stored: integer, the default, is a bigint, and double is
a double precision, which keeps a fraction. Refused on any other type:
min, max and last take the source column's type.

additionalProperties.description: RollupMeasure is one kept value and how it merges.

measures.description: Measures keyed by the column name they get in every table of the set.

items.description: RollupDimensionSet is one table per grain: a time bucket, some dimensions, and the measures kept for each.

dimension_sets.description:
The dimensions and measures kept at every grain. Each set gets one
table per grain, named <set>_<grain>.

catalog.description: The catalog serve.yml's commands attach the database as, such as pg.

max_buckets.description:
The most buckets one response may carry at any grain. Each grain's
max_range divided by its width must not exceed it.

dimension_set.description: The dimension set the dataset reads. At most one dimension.

default_range.description: The width a request gets without since, such as 24h.

max_range.description: The grains served, each with the widest range it serves.

dimension.description: The dimension folded. It must be the dimension set's dimension.

rank_by.description:
The sum measure that ranks the dimension's values. Optional when the
set has exactly one sum measure.

default.description: The series a request gets without top.

max.description: The most series a request may ask for. A larger top is refused.

top.description: How many values keep their own series.

fold.description:
Keeps the top values of the dimension as their own series and sums the
rest into "other". Required when the set has a dimension.

filters.description:
Params that filter the dimension to one value, never folded, keyed by
param name.

cache_ttl_seconds.description:
Opts the generated dataset into serve's response cache, for this many
seconds. 0 leaves it out. The generated SQL reads the range half-open,
which is what the cache's key needs.

cache_ttl_by_grain.description:
Grains that hold their answers for their own number of seconds, such
as {1d: 600}: a year of days changes by one open bucket, and re-running
the widest query every cache_ttl_seconds buys nothing a chart can show.
Needs cache_ttl_seconds, which the other grains take.

items.description: RollupDataset is one generated serve dataset.

serve.description: The serve datasets to generate. Omit to generate tables only.

items.description: Rollup is one source table and the coarser tables kept from it.

description: RollupsConf is a whole rollups file.
